message.create_linear_engineering.assemb: Assembly refused: unloaded/immovable blocks, over 2048 blocks, or beyond 64 blocks from the carriage.
message.create_linear_engineering.couple: Select a carriage on a Sable body.
First carriage selected. Click the second with the wrench to unite both bodies. Shift-click cancels.
Carriages united into one Sable body.
Add the door blocks: both bodies must touch to stay joined.
Cannot merge a rail support with its own moving carriage.
Align the two bodies on the same block grid before joining.
Joining refused: blocks would overlap or leave the target plot.
Joining refused: at most 2048 moved blocks; bounding-box volume must not exceed 129 cubed.
Joining refused: part of the body is not loaded.
Sable could not complete the transfer. Check the server log.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.horizon: Click a surface with the Linear Rail. Its base follows the face you click.
Aim at the existing guide: Create's arrow and preview extend it with matching orientation. Hold Shift to bypass assistance.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.carriag: Click the rail with a Linear Carriage. It appears already fitted around the T profile, as a physical Sable body.
Carriages can only be installed on rails. Add your payload directly to the moving body.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.physics: A level guide does not drive itself. Sable handles mass, gravity and collisions; no rotational power is required.
An external force can slide the body along the guide. The joint prevents sideways motion and rotation.
There is no invisible end stop: once fully off the rail, the body is free. Use a solid block as a physical stop.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.vertica: On a vertical guide, an unsupported carriage slides down under its own weight.
A solid block at the bottom stops it by collision. Without support it can leave the guide.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.orienta: Floor, ceiling, walls and moving structures
The clicked face determines the base. Adjacent rails preserve the orientation of the line.
Click the underside of a ceiling to hang the rail with its profile pointing down: ideal for sliding doors.
Wall mounting also works. The same mechanism works on moving or rotated Sable bodies, following their local axes.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.couplin: One rigid door on several guides
Build the door between the carriages so the bodies touch by a face. Align them on the same block grid without overlaps.
Click the first carriage, then the second with Create's wrench. Both become one rigid body, retaining their rail joints.
You can add more carriages: there is no fixed limit of two. Each merge moves at most 2048 blocks; all guides must allow the same motion.
Shift-right-click a rail or carriage with the wrench to cancel selection. Breaking the physical connection lets Sable separate the parts again.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.reentry: A detached carriage remains a physical body. Bring it back to a rail with matching axis and mounting face.
When the profiles meet in alignment, the joint reconnects automatically. It also works on moving rails.
It does not attract distant carriages or correct a sideways or upside-down approach.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.screw_d: Install a toothed carriage on a screw rail. Unlike the free carriage, it holds its position without rotation.
Connect a Create shaft at either end. The native kinetic network rotates every connected screw segment and drives the carriage.
Reverse the RPM to reverse travel. One revolution advances one quarter block; the fixed base does not rotate.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.screw_l: A powered vertical screw lifts its carriage against gravity. Floor, ceiling, wall and moving-body mounting are all supported.
At zero RPM, or when Create's network is overstressed, the drive holds the current position instead of sliding down.
Empty screw rails consume no stress. Carriage load increases stress; grease reduces it. Linked carriages need compatible drive directions and speeds.
create_linear_engineering.ponder.rail_se: Detecting a carriage along the track
Install a Rail Sensor on any free or screw rail. It shares the existing block and leaves the carriage path clear.
Approximate mode activates as soon as any part of the carriage overlaps this rail segment. Signal strength is 15, only through the back of the base.
Lamps behind successive sensors follow the carriage. During a transition, Approximate mode can detect the overlap on two neighbouring segments.
Shift-right-click with a Create wrench to select Precise mode. It activates only within 1/32 block of the segment centre, not while the carriage is offset.
Fast crossings also trigger the sensor, with a pulse of at least two game ticks. Use the signal in your door circuit: the sensor is not an automatic precision brake.
The base side remains the output on walls, ceilings and moving bodies. Breaking the rail in survival drops both the rail and its installed sensor.
tooltip.create_linear_engineering.grease: Carriages only. No added friction; screw stress reduced to 1/16.
Carriages only. Half friction; screw stress reduced to 1/4.
A dry free carriage brakes strongly. Lubrication changes its inner sliding surfaces and remains until replaced.
High Viscosity Grease halves the added brake. Amber surfaces identify the controlled sliding mode.
Low Viscosity Grease removes the added brake. Pale surfaces identify free sliding; Sable still handles contacts and drag.
On screws, High reduces stress to one quarter and Low to one sixteenth. More carried mass needs more stress; an empty rail costs none.
Even lubricated, a screw carriage holds at zero RPM. Linked carriages share their body's mass instead of counting it twice.
